title: [Afterpay] AMD Ryzen 7 5800X3D CPU $498.95 Delivered @ Centre Com eBay
body:

[Bammers] The rest of the machine is well specced (was my old desktop) It has 32gb ram and a 3080. Just figure the cpu must be getting close to 5+ years old?
[Count Shagula] 5500x3d from aliex for 200-220 will be a huge upgrade if you have a high hz monitor. I had a similar system and a 9070xt was a huge upgrade from my 10gig 3080
[SetTheFaqUp] Makes the Ryzen 10 Aurora deal look very very very cheap.
[p1 ama] This just doesn't make sense to me.
From the "DDR4 is cheaper than DDR5" angle, it doesn't make sense. Just using CentreCom as a reference, the cheapest kit of 32GB DDR4 is $349 (see: https://www.centrecom.com.au/gskill-ripjaws-v-32gb-2x16gb-dd… ), and the cheapest kit of 32GB DDR5 is $599 (see: https://www.centrecom.com.au/lexar-thor-2nd-gen-ld5u16g60c38… ) - so you save $250 on DDR4 vs. DDR5
The 5800X is slower than the 7600X is almost all tasks (see: https://www.techspot.com/review/2534-amd-ryzen-7600x/ ), if you are primarily gaming, look at the 12 game average, where the 7600X averages 211fps, and the 5800X averages 203fps. This difference is only going to be wider today as new games take better advantage of the newer architecture.
Today, the 7600X is $299 (see: https://www.centrecom.com.au/amd-ryzen-5-7600x-6-cores-12-th… ), or you can get the 7500F, which is on par with the 5800X in gaming, and superior in almost everything else for $239 (see: https://www.centrecom.com.au/amd-ryzen-5-7500f-6-cores-12-th… )
That is, 7600X + 32GB DDR5 = $898, 7500F + 32GB DDR5 = $838, 5800X + 32GB DDR4 = $848.
Even if you have a current AM4 board, decent AM5 boards are cheap as chips these days (e.g. https://www.centrecom.com.au/gigabyte-b650m-gaming-plus-wi-f… ) - at $159.
Obviously I think most should purchase the 7500F + 32GB DDR5, which is cheaper, better, and actually has an upgrade path. You can upgrade all the way to a 9950X3D, your DDR5 will last you at least 2 more generations of upgrades and you get all of the latest platform features.
The only reason you should buy this is if you happen to have 32GB+ of DDR4 just lying around, but even in that case, I would just HODL for now rather than paying $500 for an old CPU that is outperformed by the 7500F.
